names.name: The proof box
names.said: Warm, damp, and the one thing in the shop nobody opens without a reason.

text.what: A warm humid cabinet where cut rings take their final rise before they go in the fat.
text.story: *Tradition holds —* a proof box is run warm and wet so the skin does not dry: a dried skin will not expand and the ring fries lopsided. Shops without a box use a rack near the fryer and the room's own heat, which is why a raised dough behaves differently in January.
text.how: Rings go in on screens, come out when they wobble.
text.today: The box is the piece of equipment that decides whether a shop can run raised dough at volume.
